pinyin: qiān chuí bǎi liàn chéng zhēn jīn
literal: thousand · hammerings · hundred · smeltings · become · true · gold
natural: A thousand hammerings and a hundred smeltings make true gold

meaning.en: Only through repeated hardship and training do people become truly capable.
meaning.zh: 经过反复磨炼，才能成为真正有本事的人。

examples.zh: 千锤百炼成真金，这些年的磨炼让他成熟了。
examples.en: Thousands of hammerings make true gold; those years of training have matured him.

examples.zh: 千锤百炼成真金，新兵只有经历严格训练才能成长。
examples.en: Recruits only grow through strict training.

usage.en: Often paired with 烈火炼真金. Used in encouragement and commendation.
usage.zh: 常用于鼓励和表彰。

text: 是骡子是马，拉出来遛遛
pinyin: shì luó zi shì mǎ, lā chū lái liù liù
variants: 是骡子是马拉出来遛遛
是骡子是马，牵出来遛遛
literal: is · mule · is · horse, pull · out · come · walk around
natural: Whether it's a mule or a horse, lead it out and see

meaning.en: Prove your ability by action and let the results speak.
meaning.zh: 到底有没有本事，拿出来试一试就知道。

equivalents: The proof of the pudding is in the eating

examples.zh: 是骡子是马，拉出来遛遛，咱们比一比就知道。
examples.en: Mule or horse, lead it out and see; a contest will show.

examples.zh: 是骡子是马，拉出来遛遛，光说不练可不行。
examples.en: Mule or horse, let's see; talk without action won't do.

usage.en: A challenge to someone boasting. 遛 is liù (to walk an animal).
usage.zh: 用于向吹嘘的人挑战。“遛”读 liù。

text: 是福不是祸，是祸躲不过
pinyin: shì fú bù shì huò, shì huò duǒ bù guò
literal: if · blessing · not · calamity, if · calamity · hide · not · past
natural: If it's a blessing it's not a disaster; if it's a disaster you can't avoid it

meaning.en: Accept whatever fate brings, for you can't escape misfortune.
meaning.zh: 是福就不是祸，是祸也躲不开，劝人坦然面对。

examples.zh: 是福不是祸，是祸躲不过，别太担心了。
examples.en: Blessing or disaster, what will come will come; don't worry too much.

examples.zh: 是福不是祸，是祸躲不过，我们只能面对。
examples.en: We can only face it; if it's a calamity we can't avoid it.

usage.en: Philosophical or fatalistic; used to comfort or to resign oneself.
usage.zh: 带哲理或宿命色彩，用于宽慰或认命。

text: 是非只为多开口，烦恼皆因强出头
pinyin: shì fēi zhǐ wèi duō kāi kǒu, fán nǎo jiē yīn qiǎng chū tóu
literal: disputes · only · because · more · open · mouth, worries · all · because · force · stick out · head
natural: Trouble comes from speaking too much, worries from pushing yourself forward

meaning.en: Stay quiet and don't push yourself forward, and you'll avoid trouble.
meaning.zh: 少说话、不强出头，就能避免是非烦恼。

equivalents: Speech is silver, silence is golden

examples.zh: 是非只为多开口，烦恼皆因强出头，他一向谨言慎行。
examples.en: Trouble is from speaking too much; he's always careful in speech.

examples.zh: 是非只为多开口，烦恼皆因强出头，开会时少说两句吧。
examples.en: Say a little less in the meeting; trouble comes from talking too much.

usage.en: A cautious, somewhat passive philosophy; shortened often to the first line.
usage.zh: 处世谨慎消极的说法，常只说前半句。

pinyin: shéi jiā guō dǐ bù hēi
literal: whose · home · pot · bottom · not · black
natural: Whose pot doesn't have a black bottom?

meaning.en: Everyone has flaws or problems of their own; don't judge others.
meaning.zh: 谁家都有缺点和难处，别光说别人。

equivalents: People who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones

examples.zh: 谁家锅底不黑，你就别笑话他了。
examples.en: Every pot has a black bottom, so don't laugh at him.

examples.zh: 谁家锅底不黑，大家都有难处。
examples.en: Whose pot isn't black underneath? Everyone has troubles.

usage.en: Often a rhetorical question. Used to defend someone or deflect criticism.
usage.zh: 常以反问出现，用于为人辩护。

text: 谁人背后无人说，谁人背后不说人
pinyin: shéi rén bèi hòu wú rén shuō, shéi rén bèi hòu bù shuō rén
literal: who · behind · back · no · one · speak, who · behind · back · not · talk about · people
natural: Who isn't talked about behind their back, and who doesn't talk about others?

meaning.en: Everyone gossips and is gossiped about, so don't take it to heart.
meaning.zh: 谁都会被人在背后议论，谁也会在背后议论别人，不必介意。

examples.zh: 谁人背后无人说，谁人背后不说人，别太在意他们的闲话。
examples.en: Who isn't talked about, and who doesn't talk? Don't mind their gossip.

examples.zh: 谁人背后无人说，谁人背后不说人，想开点。
examples.en: Everyone is discussed behind their back; take it lightly.

usage.en: Often used to comfort someone who is being gossiped about.
usage.zh: 常用来安慰被人议论的人。

pinyin: jī shàn zhī jiā, bì yǒu yú qìng
literal: accumulate · good · 's · family, surely · have · surplus · blessings
natural: A family that accumulates good deeds will surely have blessings to spare

meaning.en: Doing good brings happiness to a family and its descendants.
meaning.zh: 多做善事的人家，福泽会延及子孙。

equivalents: Do good and good will follow

examples.zh: 积善之家，必有余庆，他家几代人乐善好施。
examples.en: A family that does good will have blessings to spare; generations of his family have been generous.

examples.zh: 积善之家，必有余庆，多做好事总没错。
examples.en: You can't go wrong doing good deeds; good families are blessed.

story.en: The Commentary on Words of the Book of Changes says a family that accumulates good will have surplus blessings, one that accumulates evil surplus misfortune.
story.zh: 《周易·坤·文言》：“积善之家，必有余庆；积不善之家，必有余殃。”

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前9—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 9th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: Usually followed by 积不善之家，必有余殃. Common on family couplets and in moral advice.
usage.zh: 下句常为“积不善之家，必有余殃”。常用于家训和劝善。

pinyin: zāo kāng zhī qī bù xià táng
literal: dregs · chaff · 's · wife · not · descend · hall
natural: A wife who shared one's hard times must not be sent away

meaning.en: A man should not abandon the wife who shared his poverty.
meaning.zh: 共患难的妻子不能抛弃。

equivalents: Stand by those who stood by you

examples.zh: 糟糠之妻不下堂，富贵之后也不能忘了她。
examples.en: A wife of hard times must not be cast aside; he shouldn't forget her once rich.

examples.zh: 糟糠之妻不下堂，他拒绝了高官的联姻。
examples.en: He refused the marriage offer from a high official, remaining loyal to his wife.

story.en: When Emperor Guangwu hinted that Song Hong should divorce his wife to marry a princess, Song Hong replied that a friend from poverty must not be forgotten and a wife of 糟糠 must not be sent from the hall.
story.zh: 宋弘对光武帝说：“臣闻贫贱之知不可忘，糟糠之妻不下堂。”

usage.en: Attributed to Song Hong in the Eastern Han; 糟糠 (dregs and chaff) stands for poor food.
usage.zh: 相传出自东汉宋弘，糟糠指粗劣的食物，喻贫贱。

pinyin: yǒu yǎn bù shí tài shān
literal: have · eyes · not · recognise · Mount Tai
natural: Having eyes but not recognising Mount Tai

meaning.en: To fail to recognise an eminent person; used as an apology.
meaning.zh: 有眼睛却认不出泰山，表示没认出地位高或本事大的人。

equivalents: I didn't realise who you were

examples.zh: 原来您就是总经理，真是有眼不识泰山！
examples.en: So you're the general manager; I failed to recognise you, please forgive me!

examples.zh: 我有眼不识泰山，刚才多有冒犯。
examples.en: I'm sorry for failing to recognise an eminent person; forgive my rudeness earlier.

usage.en: Usually self-reproachful and polite. Sometimes jokingly.
usage.zh: 多作自责客套，有时开玩笑。

pinyin: yī gè jiāng jūn yī gè lìng
literal: one · general · one · order
natural: Each general gives his own orders

meaning.en: A new leader brings new rules, and the old ones are replaced.
meaning.zh: 换了一个领导，就有一套新的指令和做法。

examples.zh: 一个将军一个令，新主管上任后流程全变了。
examples.en: A new boss, a new set of orders; the processes all changed after the new manager arrived.

examples.zh: 一个将军一个令，我们得适应新领导的风格。
examples.en: Each general has his own command; we must adapt to the new leader's style.

usage.en: Neutral-to-wry comment on new management. Often paired with 一朝天子一朝臣.
usage.zh: 对新领导上任的感叹，常与“一朝天子一朝臣”并用。

pinyin: bù dào huǒ hòu bù jiē guō
literal: not · reach · cooking time · not · lift · lid
natural: Don't lift the lid until the heat is right

meaning.en: Wait until the time is ripe before acting; don't rush.
meaning.zh: 时机没到不要急于行动。

examples.zh: 不到火候不揭锅，现在谈判条件还不成熟。
examples.en: Don't lift the lid before it's ready; the negotiation isn't ripe yet.

examples.zh: 不到火候不揭锅，别急着公布结果。
examples.en: Don't lift the lid too early; don't rush to announce the result.

usage.en: A cooking image: lifting the lid early spoils the dish. 火候 is huǒ hou.
usage.zh: 烹饪比喻：过早揭锅会坏事。

pinyin: bié rén qiān lǘ nǐ bá jué zi
literal: others · lead · donkey · you · pull out · tethering peg
natural: Others are leading the donkey and you pull out the peg

meaning.en: To sabotage someone else's work while they're busy with it.
meaning.zh: 别人正在做事，你却从中捣乱拆台。

equivalents: To put a spoke in someone's wheel

examples.zh: 人家正在谈生意，你这不是别人牵驴你拔橛子吗？到底想干什么？
examples.en: They're negotiating a deal, and you're pulling out the peg while others lead the donkey; what are you up to?

examples.zh: 别人牵驴你拔橛子，这种拆台的事别干。
examples.en: Don't be the one who pulls out the peg while others lead the donkey; don't sabotage.

usage.en: Northern dialect saying; also with 橛 (jué, short wooden stake).
usage.zh: 北方俗语，橛指短木桩。

pinyin: zǎi mài yé tián bù xīn téng
literal: son · sell · grandpa's · land · not · feel pain
natural: The son sells grandpa's land without any heartache

meaning.en: People waste what they didn't earn themselves.
meaning.zh: 后辈挥霍祖辈留下的家产，一点也不心疼。

equivalents: Fools and their money are soon parted

examples.zh: 崽卖爷田不心疼，富二代把家产败光了。
examples.en: Sons waste grandfathers' land without pain; the heir squandered the family fortune.

examples.zh: 崽卖爷田不心疼，国家的资源也不能这么糟蹋。
examples.en: Squandering what you haven't earned is easy, but the nation's resources must not be wasted like this.

usage.en: 崽 (zǎi) is a dialect word for son. The saying criticises squandering inherited or public property.
usage.zh: “崽”是方言，指儿子。批评挥霍继承或公共的财产。

pinyin: lā bù chū shǐ lái yuàn máo fáng
literal: cannot · pass · stool · come · blame · latrine
natural: Unable to go, he blames the latrine

meaning.en: To blame outside circumstances for one's own failure.
meaning.zh: 自己做不成事，却怪外部条件不好。

equivalents: A bad workman blames his tools

examples.zh: 拉不出屎来怨茅房，成绩不好别怪老师。
examples.en: Can't go, blames the latrine; don't blame the teacher for your poor grades.

examples.zh: 你这是拉不出屎来怨茅房，问题出在你自己身上。
examples.en: You're blaming the latrine; the fault is yours.

usage.en: Crude and very casual; use among close friends.
usage.zh: 口语，较粗俗，适合熟人之间。

pinyin: jiǎn dào lán lǐ jiù shì cài
literal: pick · into · basket · inside · then · is · vegetable
natural: Whatever you pick into the basket counts as a vegetable

meaning.en: Not being choosy; accepting anything without discrimination.
meaning.zh: 不加挑选，凡是弄到手的都算数。

examples.zh: 他找对象拣到篮里就是菜，一点也不挑。
examples.en: He's not picky about partners; whatever's in the basket counts as a vegetable.

examples.zh: 采购不能拣到篮里就是菜，质量要把关。
examples.en: Buying can't be 'whatever's in the basket is a vegetable'; quality must be checked.

usage.en: Often mildly critical: lack of quality control or discrimination.
usage.zh: 多略带批评，指不加选择。

pinyin: chī bié rén jiáo guo de mó bù xiāng
literal: eat · others · chewed · steamed bread · not · tasty
natural: Bread chewed by others doesn't taste good

meaning.en: Copying others' ideas is unrewarding; originality is better.
meaning.zh: 照搬别人的东西没有意思，要有自己的创造。

examples.zh: 吃别人嚼过的馍不香，咱们要走自己的路。
examples.en: Chewed-over bread isn't tasty; we'll take our own path.

examples.zh: 吃别人嚼过的馍不香，写文章要有自己的想法。
examples.en: Don't repeat others' ideas; write with your own thoughts.

usage.en: A northern food image: 馍 (mó) is steamed bread.
usage.zh: 北方饮食比喻，馍指馒头。

pinyin: shuǐ qiǎn yǎng bù zhù dà yú
literal: water · shallow · can't · keep · big · fish
natural: Shallow water can't keep big fish

meaning.en: A small place can't hold a big talent.
meaning.zh: 小地方留不住大人才。

equivalents: A big fish needs a big pond

examples.zh: 水浅养不住大鱼，小公司留不住他这样的人才。
examples.en: A small pond can't hold a big fish; a small company can't keep talent like him.

examples.zh: 水浅养不住大鱼，他去大城市发展了。
examples.en: Shallow water can't keep big fish; he went off to a big city.

usage.en: Used to explain why talented people leave, or to urge companies to offer more.
usage.zh: 用来解释人才流失，或提醒单位提供更大平台。

pinyin: yàn zi xián ní lěi dà wō
literal: swallow · carry in beak · mud · build · big · nest
natural: Swallows carry mud in their beaks to build a big nest

meaning.en: Great things are built from small, steady efforts.
meaning.zh: 一点一点积累，坚持不懈，就能成就大事。

equivalents: Rome wasn't built in a day
Many a little makes a mickle

examples.zh: 燕子衔泥垒大窝，只要每天坚持，总会有成就。
examples.en: Swallows carry mud and build a big nest; keep going daily and you'll achieve something.

examples.zh: 燕子衔泥垒大窝，家业是一点点攒出来的。
examples.en: The family fortune was built up bit by bit, as swallows build a nest.

usage.en: Encouragement to persevere. Often used with 积少成多.
usage.zh: 用于勉励坚持，常和“积少成多”并用。

pinyin: guā wú gǔn yuán, rén wú shí quán
literal: melon · no · perfectly round, person · no · perfect
natural: No melon is perfectly round, and no one is perfect

meaning.en: Nobody is perfect, so be tolerant of faults.
meaning.zh: 没有十全十美的人，不要苛求别人。

examples.zh: 瓜无滚圆，人无十全，对同事别太苛刻。
examples.en: No melon is perfectly round, no person is perfect; don't be too harsh on colleagues.

examples.zh: 瓜无滚圆，人无十全，我也有做不好的地方。
examples.en: No one is perfect; I too have things I can't do well.

usage.en: Often with 金无足赤，人无完人 as parallel sayings.
usage.zh: 常与“金无足赤，人无完人”并用。

text: 当官不为民做主，不如回家卖红薯
pinyin: dāng guān bù wèi mín zuò zhǔ, bù rú huí jiā mài hóng shǔ
variants: 当官不为民做主不如回家卖红薯
literal: be · official · not · for · people · make decisions, better · go back · home · sell · sweet potatoes
natural: If an official doesn't act for the people, he'd do better to go home and sell sweet potatoes

meaning.en: Officials who don't serve the people should resign.
meaning.zh: 做官不为百姓办事，还不如辞官回家。

equivalents: Public office is a public trust

examples.zh: 当官不为民做主，不如回家卖红薯，这是老百姓的心声。
examples.en: If you don't serve the people, go home and sell sweet potatoes; that's what ordinary people feel.

examples.zh: 当官不为民做主，不如回家卖红薯，这句老话至今有道理。
examples.en: If an official doesn't decide for the people, he'd better sell sweet potatoes; this old saying still rings true.

usage.en: Originally an opera line; now a popular slogan about accountable officials. Also appears in stage plays.
usage.zh: 原为戏词，今成为对官员的朴素要求。

pinyin: bēi zhe bào zhe yī bān zhòng
literal: carry on back · carry in arms · equally · heavy
natural: Carried on the back or in the arms, it weighs the same

meaning.en: Whichever way you look at it, the burden is the same.
meaning.zh: 背着也好抱着也好，分量都一样，指怎么做负担都差不多。

equivalents: Six of one, half a dozen of the other

examples.zh: 背着抱着一般重，何必争论谁多干了活儿。
examples.en: Carrying on the back or in the arms weighs the same; why argue who did more?

examples.zh: 带孩子背着抱着一般重，只能自己慢慢熬。
examples.en: Carrying a child either way weighs the same; you just have to endure.

usage.en: A folk saying from child-rearing, rare outside dialect areas.
usage.zh: 源自带孩子的民间说法，主要流行于方言区。

pinyin: rùn sì yuè, chī shù yè
literal: leap · fourth · month, eat · tree · leaves
natural: In a leap fourth month people eat leaves

meaning.en: Folk belief that a leap year with a second fourth month brings a poor harvest and hunger.
meaning.zh: 民间说法：遇到闰四月，粮食歉收，人要靠吃树叶度日。

examples.zh: 老辈人说闰四月，吃树叶，那年果然闹了饥荒。
examples.en: The elders said that a leap fourth month means eating leaves, and indeed there was famine that year.

examples.zh: 闰四月，吃树叶，这是农民对天时的担心。
examples.en: A leap fourth month, eat leaves: this expresses farmers' worry about the weather.

usage.en: A regional agricultural superstition; not reliable but widely repeated in some provinces.
usage.zh: 地方性农事说法，并不可靠，部分地区流传。
